clusters.state_of_play: US Congressman Ro Khanna was detained by Israeli settlers armed with US-made M4 rifles near the Palestinian village of Khirbet Zanuta in the West Bank for 90 minutes on a Wednesday, mid-way through a three-day West Bank tour; he was released only after calls to the American Embassy in Jerusalem. IDF personnel arrived on scene, spoke with settlers, and moved a car to block the road. Khanna posted video evidence on social media of the incident. He has directly accused the IDF of siding with the settlers, calling it a 'huge mistake,' and on Sunday escalated by accusing the Israeli government and military of 'lying' about the detention. Israeli Ambassador to the US Michael Leiter has accused Khanna of staging a political stunt to distract from his support for Graham Platner. Khanna stated he is 'strongly considering' a presidential run and said the trip made him more resolved to do so. The incident is part of a pattern of Democratic presidential aspirants visiting the region to establish critic credentials. Israeli Ambassador Michael Leiter separately stated that Israel is prepared to restart war with Iran if the US requests it, amid ongoing US-Iran exchanges of fire. Separately, Qatar's sovereign wealth fund has vetoed a Volkswagen joint venture with an Israeli firm that would have produced vehicles supporting Israel's Iron Dome mobile air-defense system, threatening hundreds of jobs at a VW site. In Gaza, Israeli attacks have killed at least 1,098 Palestinians since the US-brokered ceasefire in October, including five in the latest strikes — among them a 9-year-old girl. Kamal Adwan hospital was struck by an Israeli drone, wounding health workers; power cuts are plunging Gaza hospitals into darkness. Nine months into the ceasefire, Israel now controls nearly 70% of Gaza, up from roughly 50% at ceasefire onset. The US has sent a team to Beirut to shore up the Israel-Hizbollah ceasefire, while Lebanon's president is calling for international pressure on Israel to begin withdrawing its forces. Separately, state attorneys general are preparing to file a lawsuit as soon as this week to block the $111 billion Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, posing a potential major obstacle to the deal; Paramount is also weighing leaving California amid an intensifying battle with state regulators, though David Ellison is said to be wary of decamping.

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. clusters.title: Power cuts plunge Gaza hospitals into darkness as Israel’s attacks persist

items.title: Power cuts plunge Gaza hospitals into darkness as Israel’s attacks persist

ledger.what_new: Power cuts are plunging Gaza hospitals into darkness amid ongoing Israeli bombing.
ledger.unique: Energy crisis specifically darkening Gaza hospitals mid-conflict.

clusters.state_of_play: US Congressman Ro Khanna was detained by Israeli settlers armed with US-made M4 rifles near the Palestinian village of Khirbet Zanuta in the West Bank for 90 minutes on a Wednesday, mid-way through a three-day West Bank tour; he was released only after calls to the American Embassy in Jerusalem. IDF personnel arrived on scene, spoke with settlers, and moved a car to block the road. Khanna posted video evidence on social media of the incident. He has directly accused the IDF of siding with the settlers, calling it a 'huge mistake,' and on Sunday escalated by accusing the Israeli government and military of 'lying' about the detention. Israeli Ambassador to the US Michael Leiter has accused Khanna of staging a political stunt to distract from his support for Graham Platner. Khanna stated he is 'strongly considering' a presidential run and said the trip made him more resolved to do so. The incident is part of a pattern of Democratic presidential aspirants visiting the region to establish critic credentials. Israeli Ambassador Michael Leiter separately stated that Israel is prepared to restart war with Iran if the US requests it, amid ongoing US-Iran exchanges of fire. Separately, Qatar's sovereign wealth fund has vetoed a Volkswagen joint venture with an Israeli firm that would have produced vehicles supporting Israel's Iron Dome mobile air-defense system, threatening hundreds of jobs at a VW site. In Gaza, Israeli attacks have killed at least 1,098 Palestinians since the US-brokered ceasefire in October, including five in the latest strikes — among them a 9-year-old girl. Kamal Adwan hospital was struck by an Israeli drone, wounding health workers; power cuts are plunging Gaza hospitals into darkness. Nine months into the ceasefire, Israel now controls nearly 70% of Gaza, up from roughly 50% at ceasefire onset. The US has sent a team to Beirut to shore up the Israel-Hizbollah ceasefire, while Lebanon's president is calling for international pressure on Israel to begin withdrawing its forces. clusters.state_of_play: DR Congo is experiencing its fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, with nearly 1,800 confirmed cases and over 600 deaths. Two U.S. citizens have tested positive — an American doctor earlier in the outbreak (transferred to Germany for treatment) and a second U.S. citizen working for a humanitarian organization. The CDC is coordinating with the person's employer and Congolese partners to prevent further transmission. New suspected cases have emerged in parts of Congo previously unaffected, signaling spread beyond the Ituri epicenter. Containment efforts are further threatened by health workers protesting non-payment. In a parallel development, the first patients have been enrolled in a clinical treatment trial in the Ituri region — set up in just six weeks after the outbreak was declared, a record pace — testing two drugs with hopes of reducing mortality rates. There is currently no approved drug for this Ebola outbreak.
